thread:
jamie (capacity): Heads up — Finance is re-pricing the Pro tier tomorrow morning. Early telemetry and customer comms suggest a meaningful upsell from Basic -> Pro. We need a quick capacity estimate and a short-term procurement ask for GPUs in us-west and eu-west. Can infra plz triage by EOD? :eyes:

sam (prod-econ): Running a quick sim now. Short summary: median incremental GPU need for hosted Pro endpoints looks like ~12 GPUs total (spread across regions) for a 3-week window; P95 ~20. I'll drop the back-of-envelope below.

maria (infra): Thanks — helpful. Two operational asks: 1) can we get a reserved pool request ready for procurement (spot->reserved fallback) 2) confirm any region constraints (quota, NVLink racks) for us-west1 / eu-west1. I can start the quota requests once we lock numbers.

sam (prod-econ): Paste of the quick calc (very rough):
```
Assumptions:
- baseline hosted Pro peak token/hour = 100e9 tokens
- expected uplift = +17% -> delta = 17e9 tokens/hour
- effective tokens per A100-GPU-hour (quantized mixed workload) ~ 3.2e9 tokens/GPU-hour
=> GPUs (hourly sustained) = ceil(17e9 / 3.2e9) = ~6 GPUs sustained
Add concurrency and safety (canary + burst) -> target short-term pool = 12 GPUs
P95 (heavy-week scenario) ~ 20 GPUs
Window: 3 weeks for rollout and stabilization
Estimated cloud cost (raw infra) ~ 12 GPUs * 24h * 21d * $3.5/hr ~= $21k (ballpark)
```

alok (eng-runtime): Couple of notes on the numbers: our tokens/GPU-hour varies a ton by model family and sequence length. If the uplift skews toward our chat workloads (longer generations) you can expect tokens/GPU-hour to drop ~30%. Also we can blunt the peak with short policy changes: tighten prefix caching + bump batching target for Pro routes. That could reduce incremental GPUs by ~10-15% with near-zero cost.

maria (infra): I checked quotas: us-west1 has spare quota to add up to 20 GPUs in our current project, but eu-west1 is limited (we're at 85% of regional NVLink racks for the instance type). If we need eu-west headroom we either: a) request capacity increase (lead time ~48-72h) or b) fallback to us-west for burst (adds egress latency for EU customers).

natalie (sales): Heads-up from GTM: we plan targeted emails to affected cohorts tomorrow afternoon. If we can't promise equal latency, we should gate some features in EU (or mark as "best-effort") to avoid SLA violations.

jamie (capacity): Proposed action items:
- sam: finalize Monte Carlo and produce a 3-point ask (median / p90 / p95) by 12:30pm
- maria: start quota + reserved-pool request for us-west1 and open support ticket for eu-west1 capacity; request scope: 15 GPUs us-west, 8 GPUs eu-west as conservative ask
- alok: implement two mitigation knobs (increase prefix cache TTL + conservative batching bump) as a config toggle to flip during rollout
- natalie: coordinate messaging + knob windows so we can throttle rollout if needed

maria (infra): I've opened the procurement ticket and quota requests. support ticket ID: SUP-3421. If support can get eu-west increase within 72h we should be fine; otherwise we'll route heavier Pro traffic to us-west and notify customers.

deploy-bot: support ticket SUP-3421 created: https://redwood.support/SUP-3421 -> assigned to capacity-team, priority: high

sam (prod-econ): Final note: if Finance expects sustained uplift (not just onboarding sprint) we should discuss reserved capacity contracts vs short-term cloud bursts — breakeven for reserved vs on-demand is ~6 weeks at the modeled uplift. I'll surface a cost comparison in the final deck.

jamie (capacity): Great — thanks. Please update this thread when you have the sim and support ticket progress. I'll schedule a 30m sync if any region-level blockers pop up. :+1:
